{{Quote|Among other dishonorable acts, this piece of human filth once interfered with a legitimate slaver operation on Gandolo IV.|Bossk, referring to Han Solo|<ref name="Agents">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos I: Hero's Trial]]''</ref>}}
'''Gandolo IV''' was a barren, rocky [[Moon/Legends|moon]] in the [[Gandolo system/Legends|Gandolo system]] of the [[Lahara sector/Legends|Lahara sector]], in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. By [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], a group of several dozen fugitive [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] individuals, including the famous [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], attempted to establish a safe [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] on the moon but was discovered by the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]]. Paid in advance by the [[Lahara sector Imperial governor|Imperial sector governor]], Bossk and a team of hunters landed on Gandolo IV to capture the renegade Wookiees. The [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] proved particularly opportunistic for Bossk, who finally got a chance to capture Chewbacca after the Wookiee had continuously eluded him for some [[Time/Legends|time]]. Before the Trandoshan could secure his quarry, however, Chewbacca's [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] partner, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], returned to Gandolo IV from business elsewhere to find the Wookiees detained. Careful not to harm Chewbacca and the other Wookiees, Solo strafed the camp in the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] and proceeded to land his [[Starship/Legends|ship]] directly on top of Bossk's own [[Bossk's freighter|ship]], crushing it. The Wookiees overpowered Bossk's group in the mayhem.

Although the Wookiees were forced to abandon their colonization effort, Solo and Chewbacca promised to help them set up a new colony elsewhere. The incident turned into an utter humiliation for Bossk, whom Solo and Chewbacca had left trapped in his ruined ship, rather than killing him. Bossk, determined to avenge himself for the embarrassment, would be painfully reminded of the Gandolo IV fiasco on occasion for the next twenty-five [[Standard year/Legends|years]].

==Description==
Gandolo IV was a barren, rocky [[Moon/Legends|moon]]<ref name="CSWE" /> located in the distant [[Lahara sector/Legends|Lahara sector's]] [[Gandolo system/Legends|Gandolo system]],<ref name="Essential Atlas Online Companion" /> within the north-eastern quadrant of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> part of the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]].<ref name="Region" /> Its surface pockmarked with large craters, Gandolo IV appeared [[Color/Legends|gray]] and lifeless from [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="SWR">[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']]</ref>

==History==
===The Wookiee colony===
{{Quote|Bossk&hellip;had a personal grudge against Chewbacca&hellip;to capture the mighty Wookiee would greatly add to Bossk's already formidable reputation&hellip;The bounty hunter got his chance during a visit to Gandolo IV.|Rebel Alliance historian [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]]|<ref name="GG3">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref>}}
[[File:Bossk-TCW.png|thumb|left|Bossk, who kidnapped Wookiees on Gandolo IV]]
Sometime by [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]],<ref name="SWTCC">''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]'' establishes [[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika|''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'']] was one [[in-universe]] [[Standard year/Legends|year]] before [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which is in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. This places ''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'' in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], and ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' establishes [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] had his encounter with [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] on Gandolo IV prior to the events of ''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika''.</ref> a group of several dozen renegade [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] led by [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] set up a safe retreat on the remote, barren moon Gandolo IV.<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> When news of the Wookiee colony's establishment reached [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], a successful [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], he jumped at the opportunity to [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] down the [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]]. Bossk harbored a vile hatred of Wookiees, with whom his [[Species/Legends|species]] shared the [[Kashyyyk system/Legends|Kashyyyk system]], as well a [[Blood/Legends|blood]] feud after the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] declared Wookiees to be [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] at the behest of a Trandoshan dignitary during the early [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]]. Bossk was among the Trandoshans vowing to help bring all fugitive Wookiees to Imperial justice.<ref name="GG3" /> Despite his successes at hunting Wookiees, he most desired to capture the elusive Chewbacca, who, along with his [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] partner, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], had earned quite a reputation among the criminal underworld.<ref name="EGC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

Chewbacca refused to present himself to his Trandoshan pursuer, but Bossk's opportunity came at Gandolo IV. After the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunter first visited the Lahara [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] [[Lahara sector Imperial governor|Imperial governor]] in order to be paid in advance for the bounty on the Wookiee colonists, Bossk and a handful of fellow hirelings armed themselves for the trip to Gandolo IV, where they found their quarry. A group of poorly armed Wookiees was setting up a small outpost on the barren moon with the assistance of Chewbacca himself.<ref name="EGC" />

Bossk's group, greatly outnumbering their prey, easily surrounded and captured the camp, catching the Wookiees almost completely by surprise.<ref name="EGC" /> With their captives in [[Binders/Legends|binders]],<ref name="GG3" /> the hunters were on the verge of skinning the Wookiees<ref name="Bossk">{{StoryCite|story=The Prize Pelt: The Tale of Bossk|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> when Han Solo arrived on the scene. Solo had previously dropped Chewbacca off on Gandolo IV before proceeding to a nearby [[Star system/Legends|star system]] to visit an old girlfriend.<ref name="EGC" /> The [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]], [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], returned only to detect the bounty hunters' ship from low [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]], and he knew something was wrong.<ref name="GG3" />

===Rescuing the Wookiees===
Solo dropped in on the camp unannounced, strafing low over the confused bounty hunters with a hail of [[Laser/Legends|laser]] fire from the ''Millennium Falcon''. Knowing he couldn't directly attack the hunters for risk of hitting the bound Wookiees, Solo was careful to shoot only the ground, which sent Bossk and his crew scattering for their own [[Bossk's freighter|ship]].<ref name="EGC" /> Although the Trandoshan's craft was larger and better armed than his own,<ref name="Bossk" /> Solo had already outwitted them. As soon as Bossk had raised his [[Entry ramp/Legends|boarding ramp]], Solo lowered his landing gear and brought the ''Millennium Falcon'' directly down upon the bounty hunter's ship. The additional weight of Solo's [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] buckled the landing struts of Bossk's ship in a collapsed heap of explosions and a cloud of shot hydraulic fluids.<ref name="EGC" /> When Solo lifted the ''Millennium Falcon'' off the ruined ship, it rolled over onto its side, a wrecked heap.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:HanSolo.png|thumb|right|220px|Han Solo, the Wookiees' rescuer]]
Bossk and his team tried desperately to open the emergency hatches of the ship, to no avail.<ref name="EGC" /> In the confusion, Chewbacca and the Wookiees escaped their captors. They broke free of their binders, dispatched the two bounty hunters guarding them, and proceeded to neutralize the rest of the group before knocking out the drive and weapons systems of Bossk's ship.<ref name="GG3" /> Solo and Chewbacca left Gandolo IV behind, promising to help the rest of the Wookiees find a new place to establish a safe colony. They refused to kill Bossk, however, leaving him and the bounty hunters trapped in their damaged ship.<ref name="EGC" />

Only Bossk's natural regenerative ability to regrow lost [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] saved him from Solo's ambush.<ref name="GG3" /> It took he and his companions several days to finally work their way out of their crushed ship with a few [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and [[hand torch]]es. A [[Standard week/Legends|week]] later, they were rescued from Gandolo IV's barren surface by a small out-world [[Transport/Legends|hauler]] transporting [[Nerf/Legends|nerf]] manure.<ref name="EGC" /> The Gandolo IV incident proved a bitter humiliation for Bossk, and a rare setback. He had lost his ship, his Imperial bounty on the fugitive Wookiees, but more importantly, he had lost his chance at capturing Chewbacca. The embarrassment that Solo had caused him also inspired in the Trandoshan a strong desire to one day seek vengeance on the Corellian smuggler.<ref name="GG3" />

===Bossk's continued humiliation===
Bossk's humiliation at Gandolo IV would stay with him for [[Standard year/Legends|years]], and he yearned for retribution. When [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] summoned an elite group of bounty hunters, including Bossk, to his [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]], the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], in the wake of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]<ref name="Bossk" /> in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> to capture Han Solo and his [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] companions, the Trandoshan formed an unorthodox partnership with fellow bounty hunters [[Tinian I'att Azur-Jamin|Tinian I'att]] and the Wookiee [[Chenlambec]]. The trio agreed on an uneasy alliance to capture Solo and Chewbacca&mdash;in reality a ruse by I'att and Chenlambec to capture Bossk&mdash;by tracking them to the planet [[Lomabu III]]. During their negotiations, I'att surreptitiously mocked Bossk by casually mentioning to him that she and Chenlambec and heard something about the Gandolo IV incident, which irked the Trandoshan. In fact, Chenlambec's own [[Chenlambec's brother|brother]] had been among Gandolo IV's Wookiee colonists, standing next to Chewbacca as they watched their situation turn from disaster to success, and then utter hilarity at the expense of Bossk's group.<ref name="Bossk" />

[[File:TinianIatt-Journal4.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Tinian I'att would mock Bossk for what happened to the latter on Gandolo IV]]
I'att's and Chenlambec's cover story involved telling Bossk of a safe colony a group of Wookiees was attempting to set up on Lomabu III, not unlike that of Gandolo IV. However, the situation on Lomabu III was quite the opposite. The planet was actually the site of an Imperial [[Prison/Legends|prison]] camp containing several hundred Wookiees, which would correspond closely to the former layout of Gandolo IV's outpost, as Chenlambec related to I'att. Although Bossk hoped to manipulate the situation by tricking Chenlambec into wiping out his own kin in the purported Wookiee colony, thus avenging himself for Gandolo IV, I'att and Chenlambec double-crossed him and rescued the Wookiee prisoners.<ref name="Bossk" />

Gandolo IV was still a sore subject for Bossk many years later.<ref name="Agents" /> In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Bossk once more encountered Solo on the [[Jubilee Wheel (space station)|''Jubilee Wheel'']],<ref name="Agents" /> a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] orbiting the planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]]. Chewbacca had recently [[Destruction of Sernpidal|died]] on the planet [[Sernpidal/Legends|Sernpidal]].<ref name="Essential Atlas" /> Bossk mocked Solo for his loss, citing the anger he still felt for the humiliation he was dealt on Gandolo IV. Solo gloated in return, remembering well how he landed the ''Millennium Falcon'' on top of Bossk's ship, crushing it, much to Bossk's mortification.<ref name="Agents" />

==Locations==
By 1 BBY,<ref name="SWTCC" /> several dozen fugitive Wookiee enslaved individuals attempted to establish a safe colony on Gandolo IV, free from [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] Imperial-motivated persecutions. After Bossk and his bounty hunting entourage discovered and attacked the colony, the Wookiees abandoned their efforts on Gandolo IV with Han Solo's and Chewbacca's promise that they would help the refugees find a new location for safe haven.<ref name="EGC" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Notable appearances===
The moon Gandolo IV was created for the [[1989]] first edition of the [[West End Games]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', written by [[Michael Stern]].<ref name="GG3" /> Gandolo IV also appears as one of 200 playable worlds in the [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|PC game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], which provided the planet's only [[canon]]ical visual depiction to date, an illustration as a rocky moon in accordance with Gandolo IV's original physical description from ''Galaxy Guide 3'' in 1989. The image used for Gandolo IV, however, is replicated in use with sixteen other planets of similar barren composition in the game.<ref name="SWR" />

===Inconsistencies===
''Star Wars: Rebellion''<ref name="SWR" /> and ''[[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]'' place Gandolo IV in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]] of the Outer Rim, relatively close to the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]].<ref name="Rebellion Guide">[[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Rebellion'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> This geographical placement has since been overridden by the [[2009]] release of ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', which also places the moon in grid square M-5,<ref name="Essential Atlas" /> and its related online material on [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="Essential Atlas Online Companion" />

Additionally, the ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' in-game encyclopedia seemingly refers to the Gandolo IV Wookiee colony as existing concurrently with the chronological start time of the game, which begins after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="SWR" /> This time frame has since been overridden by the [[2002]] ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'', which places the Gandolo IV incident prior to the events taking place in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika|''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'']].<ref name="NEGC" /> That comic's release dates ranged from [[December 13]], [[2000]]<ref name="DarkHorse-1">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/00-274/Star-Wars-Underworld-1-of-5|text=Star Wars: Underworld #1 (of 5)}}</ref> to [[June 20]], [[2001]].<ref name="DarkHorse-2">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/00-298/Star-Wars-Underworld-5-of-5|text=Star Wars: Underworld 5}}</ref> The [[2006]] ''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]'' established the events of that comic were one year prior to the Battle of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]].<ref name="EGC" /> 

The [[2008]] ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' explains in the "Gandolo IV" entry that Han Solo lands the ''Millennium Falcon'' on top of an Imperial troopship during the incident with Bossk, killing all aboard.<ref name="CSWE" /> As presented elsewhere in the [[in-universe]] portions of this article, that entry contradicts with other established canon, and is effectively an error.
